s1.syndrome_frame: A syndrome of severe fatigue, muscular weakness, and cachexia with a large tumor on the distal part of the right fourth finger, associated with hypercalcemia, hypophosphatemia, and elevated parathyroid hormone levels
salient_findings: Large tumor on the distal part of the right fourth finger
key_facts: Patient is a man in his 60s
History of primary hyperparathyroidism 6 years prior to presentation
Patient refused therapeutic management for primary hyperparathyroidism
Patient is cachectic
Significant muscular weakness
Large tumor on the distal part of the right fourth finger
Hypercalcemia at 3.6 mmol/L
Hypophosphatemia at 0.65 mmol/L
Elevated serum parathyroid hormone at 380 pmol/L
Radiography showed complete lysis of the underlying phalanx and periosteal bone resorption
Chest radiograph revealed important deformation of the ribs
Thoracic CT scan revealed multiple lesions associated with multiple rib and vertebral fractures
Skull radiography showed pattern of trabecular resorption with 'salt-and-pepper' appearance

shortlist.label: Brown tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathology of finger tumor shows fibrous tissue, woven bone, and giant cells, consistent with brown tumor

shortlist.label: Primary hyperparathyroidism
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated serum parathyroid hormone and hypercalcemia, with history of primary hyperparathyroidism

shortlist.label: Hyperparathyroidism-jaw tumor syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of a large tumor on the distal part of the right fourth finger, with hyperparathyroidism and jaw tumor syndrome being a possible diagnosis

shortlist.label: Osteitis fibrosa cystica
shortlist.why_kept: Radiography showed complete lysis of the underlying phalanx and periosteal bone resorption, consistent with osteitis fibrosa cystica

shortlist.label: Giant cell tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathology of finger tumor shows giant cells, which is a characteristic feature of giant cell tumor

raw.rationale: The patient's history of primary hyperparathyroidism, hypercalcemia, hypophosphatemia, and elevated serum parathyroid hormone, combined with the presence of a large tumor on the distal part of the right fourth finger and radiographic findings of bone resorption, are consistent with the development of a brown tumor, a known complication of hyperparathyroidism.

rejected.label: Primary hyperparathyroidism
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of primary hyperparathyroidism, this is not a tumor diagnosis, but rather an underlying condition that led to the development of the brown tumor.

rejected.label: Hyperparathyroidism-jaw tumor syndrome
rejected.why: This condition is characterized by the presence of jaw tumors, which is not the case in this patient, who has a tumor on the distal part of the right fourth finger.

rejected.label: Osteitis fibrosa cystica
rejected.why: While this condition is also associated with hyperparathyroidism, it is a more generalized skeletal disorder, and the patient's presentation is more consistent with a localized tumor, such as a brown tumor.

rejected.label: Giant cell tumor
rejected.why: Although the histopathology of the tumor shows giant cells, the clinical and radiographic findings are more consistent with a brown tumor, which is a specific type of tumor associated with hyperparathyroidism.

gold: Brown tumor secondary to primary hyperparathyroidism due to parathyroid carcinoma
